observations.note: The historical basin is documented at the spring on the tell’s eastern foot. This is a qualitative source relation; no basin-to-anchor surveyed bearing is asserted.
observations.reference_frame: Dorrell’s qualitative spring/tell description; unregistered historical photographs

observations.note: The 1898 reservoir stands at the eastern-foot spring. Its position cannot supply an earlier pool state.
The irregular basin is observed in nineteenth-century records; its construction and early accessible-use interval are unknown. Do not backdate it from the adjacent ancient curved wall.
Dorrell p. 111 dates extension of the mill-pool into the present reservoir to 1898. This is a separate physical/state assignment from the historical irregular basin.

value.attributed_date: very probably late Roman or Byzantine
value.dating_basis: architectural opinion; no sealed construction date

observations.note: Late Roman / Byzantine is Dorrell’s architectural opinion, without sealed finds dating the lowest course. It does not date the separate basin.
NS1 is reported on the camp outskirts toward Khirbet Mefjar, north of the tell. No plan or surveyed cistern-mouth position was made.
observations.reference_frame: Kenyon II qualitative location; no mouth coordinate

observations.note: Kenyon labels NS1 a Roman cistern and reports Herodian lamps / comparison finds. Its construction, ancient mouth and independently dated accessible-use interval are not documented.
Area D is inferred to be in the sector north of the tell from the reviewed distribution map. This source-plan sector inference is not a measured shaft-mouth bearing.
observations.reference_frame: Fig. 91 p. 168 qualitative sector interpretation; not registered

value.attributed_date: Middle Bronze shaft with Roman burial reuse

observations.note: A Roman burial cuts into the side of a Middle Bronze shaft. The older shaft’s dated accessibility / opening arrangement in the selected early window remains unknown.
D9’s burial is at a recessed ledge at the base / side of the older shaft. This cannot be substituted for tombs at a separately defined pit mouth.
About eighteen graves are reported on the north slope / Trench II, mostly toward its northern end; not every grave has an individual mapped mouth.
observations.reference_frame: Trench II / Site O local excavation coordinates; no national datum

value.dating_basis: type comparison; no grave-associated dating finds in III 173–174

observations.note: Kenyon assigns the on-tell graves to the first century CE by grave-type comparison. There are no offerings in this scope and no dated jointly accessible grave/pit-mouth interval.
Numerous later pits occupy much of the northern trench end. Their individual mouths have no national-datum position.
observations.reference_frame: Trench II / Site O local frame

observations.note: The phase-lxxvii quarry pits cut phase-lxxvi graves and are rubble-filled. They have no secure absolute date; later-than-grave alone is not an early-window failure.
The pits truncate the graves and belong to later phase lxxvii, after grave phase lxxvi. This rejects same-phase construction only; it does not settle later joint accessibility.
Published truncation establishes sequence, not whether a usable later opening and surviving graves were jointly accessible within an early window.

On this named crypt-basin/spring assignment, the church is at the western foot and the spring southwest of the tell. This conditional crosswalk contradicts east-of-tell; it does not locate Kallai’s separate pool.
observations.reference_frame: Published qualitative church/spring/tell crosswalk; no validated bearing

observations.note: The basin was beneath a Byzantine church crypt; the church was later destroyed. The basin itself has no separate construction date or early-use interval.
Kallai’s original pp. 172–173 remain unread and the reported rock-cut pool remains unlocated. HA 76 p. 19 describes settlement excavation and supplies no pool or bearing.
No dated pool phase or physical crosswalk to the crypt basin is established; Kallai’s native pool pages remain unread.
Dhahr Mirzbaneh’s shaft tombs are documented north/NNE of the tell and attributed to Intermediate Bronze / Middle Bronze. Their ancient mouths and later accessibility are unobserved here.

value.attributed_date: Intermediate Bronze / Middle Bronze; later accessible use unknown

observations.note: Bronze Age construction does not establish or exclude survival/accessibility in the early Roman window. There is no dated pit-mouth relation to this group.
Roman–Byzantine dams and aqueducts are reported at Kh. Samiya south/SE of the tell. No surveyed contact to Kallai’s pool or the church crypt basin is established.
The inspected Kh. Yanun site record describes no pit/cistern/tomb. This is report coverage, not an archaeological absence; a pit role remains unassigned.
Rock-cut dividing pillar reported on p. 63; its cutting date is unresolved.
A pillar does not decide the retained platform/terrace reading.
